I have completed all tasks to harden the infrastructure deployment for the Python API, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Nginx stack:

The deployment was hardened by stripping all hardcoded credentials and removing public port exposures for the database, cache, and internal API; updating the Dockerfile to run as a dedicated non-root user with `python:3.13-slim`, reproducible cached installation of pinned dependencies from `requirements.txt`, built-in container health checking, and Gunicorn as the production WSGI server; configuring Docker Compose with explicit network segmentation (`frontend` and internal `backend`), healthcheck-gated startup dependencies (`service_healthy`), persistent named volumes for PostgreSQL and Redis, log rotation, resource limits, and environment variable parameterization via `.env.example`; configuring Nginx with JSON API proxy headers, connection keepalives, payload limits, security headers, and strict timeouts; authoring an operational [RUNBOOK.md](file:///tmp/claude-1000/-home-arda-projects-agent-evaluation/8413ce30-b544-4ae4-afd6-5f8333042ec1/scratchpad/agent-eval-gemini-3.1-pro/03-infra-management/RUNBOOK.md) covering startup, health verification, backup/restore, secret handling, and rollback; and writing [RESPONSE.md](file:///tmp/claude-1000/-home-arda-projects-agent-evaluation/8413ce30-b544-4ae4-afd6-5f8333042ec1/scratchpad/agent-eval-gemini-3.1-pro/03-infra-management/RESPONSE.md) detailing the highest-risk original vulnerabilities and offline verification performed.
